title: Melting of 2D Charge Crystals Quantified with In Situ TEM
content: Charge density waves (CDW) form spontaneously in some quantum materials with structural signatures identified by superlattice peaks clearly visible with electron diffraction. Here, we show charge density waves behave like ordered charge crystals that melt when brought to elevated temperature. Using in-situ TEM diffraction, we quantify CDW melting in a 2D layer of TaS2 and show it undergoes a continuous hexatic loss of order. This ‘hexatic state’ is marked by short-range translational order and long-range orientational order. We report three signatures of CDW melting visible in the evolution of superlattice peaks: (1) q-vector contraction, (2) peak blurring, and (3) a decrease in the integrated intensity. These three features, particularly wavevector contraction, are widely observed in many incommensurate CDW systems [1-3].
